assumptions: For each (3,y), the z-interval uses max(y, floor(1/R)+1) <= z <= floor(2/R), and any z outside that interval cannot satisfy the equation; no external source was needed.

When the interval formula produced a lower bound that was not an integer, I used the exact ceiling of 1/R, not a truncated approximation; this affects no count because the test z ranges are finite and exact.
For rows y=13..18, the single integral z was verified by checking all z in the scanned interval and finding exactly one with integer w; the exact pairs are collated for the final table.
A row-context table in the final deliverable will list all scanned z for each (3,y) along with the w column, showing blanks for non-integral w.
